title: gitapex gate registry (SSOT)
description: Schema for .gitapex/ssot.json -- issue #123's self-referential registry of gitapex's own deterministic gates (hooks/CI checks) and the policy-source files they read. Holds references and routing only, never policy values (mirrors the upstream tvna/claude-md precedent's own stated constraint). label_routing/label_consumers are deliberately absent -- gitapex has no .github/label-policy.toml yet, so they are not-yet-applicable per issue #123, not an oversight. Adding a field is a schema_version bump, never a silent addition (additionalProperties is false throughout).

schema_version.description: Semver of this schema file itself. Bump on any required/additionalProperties change.

tracking_issue.description: The GitHub issue that specs this registry's schema.

status.description: Lifecycle of the registry as a whole, distinct from any single gate's own status.

phase.description: Rollout phase. phase-0 = self-referential seed of gitapex's own already-existing gates only; no label_routing, no business-domain (opa-rego) entries yet.

policy_sources.description: Files that at least one gate reads as authoritative data via policy_refs[] -- not every config-shaped file in the repo, only ones a real gate actually consumes.

gates.description: Every deterministic gate gitapex enforces on itself: development-process gates and (in a future phase) adopter-authored business-domain gates share this same array -- no split by origin.

clusters.description: cluster id -> one-line description of what the cluster groups. Every gates[].cluster value must name a key here (see gitapex_scan_ssot_schema.py's drift check).

path.description: Repo-root-relative path. May be a glob (e.g. skills/*/metadata/gitapex.yaml) when every matched file shares one schema/authority.

format.description: Serialization language only -- descriptive, not a dispatch switch (that's gates[].kind).

authority.description: Free-text prose: what this file is authoritative for.

kind.description: The sole evaluation-dispatch switch. 'native' is reserved for a GitHub-platform rule with no repo-tracked artifact at all (e.g. a branch-protection setting) -- every gate seeded in phase-0 has a real backing file, so none use it yet.

script.description: Repo-root-relative path(s) to the file(s) that actually enforce this gate (a .py/.sh script, or a .yml workflow when the enforcement logic lives inline in the workflow itself, with no separate script file). Array when a gate is genuinely enforced by more than one cooperating file (e.g. a pretooluse hook plus its CI twin).

native_rule.description: Prose description of a GitHub-native rule with no repo file (kind: native only).

rule.description: One-line statement of what this gate actually enforces, grounded in the real script's logic -- not a restatement of a CLAUDE.md bullet it may be inspired by.

planes.description: Where this gate actually runs. 'local' means it has a working-tree-only invocation a contributor can run before pushing -- the discovery signal .github/scripts/gitapex_gate_local_preflight.py selects on (issue #876). A gate carrying 'local' must also carry local_invocation; one that does not must carry local_exclusion saying why, so an unwired gate is a recorded decision rather than an invisible coverage gap.

local_invocation.description: argv list -- never a shell command string -- that runs this gate against the working tree from the repository root, for gitapex_gate_local_preflight.py. The runner executes it in exec form with no shell, but that constrains the invocation mechanism, not this value: an argv naming a shell ('sh', '-c', ...) or handing inline code to an interpreter ('python3', '-c', ...) is rejected separately by gitapex_scan_ssot_schema.py's find_local_shell_argv, so this field stays a reference to a tracked script rather than a carrier of arbitrary commands. It must also name one of this gate's own script paths (find_local_invocation_identity_drift), so a wired gate cannot report PASS without actually running. Only valid when planes contains 'local'.

local_stdin.description: argv list -- never a shell command string, same constraints as local_invocation -- whose standard output is piped into local_invocation's standard input. The one input provider this runner offers, for gates that read a unified diff on stdin. Absent for gates that need no piped input. Known limit, disclosed rather than solved: nothing here can express 'this gate REQUIRES piped input', so deleting this field from a gate that reads stdin leaves a schema-valid entry that reports PASS on an empty diff -- see gitapex_gate_local_preflight.py's own Known-limits section.

local_exclusion.description: Why this gate has no working-tree-only invocation (needs a PR/issue body, GitHub API state, a diff-derived argument, or a toolchain outside the local surface). Required exactly when planes does not contain 'local'.

trigger.description: What fires this gate: a hook matcher, a workflow event, or a pytest collection path.

policy_refs.description: policy_sources[].id values this gate reads as authoritative data. Empty when the gate's rule vocabulary is hardcoded in its own script (true for most of phase-0's seed).

tracking_issue.description: The issue(s) that introduced this specific gate. A single integer for the common case; an array of at least two issue numbers when the same gate is legitimately tracked under more than one issue (e.g. a shared umbrella issue plus the issue whose repair actually implemented it) -- a single-element array is rejected to keep the plain-integer form the only way to express one issue. null when the origin is a pre-issue-discipline squashed import, or genuinely compound (spans more than one issue) rather than guessed.

supersedes.description: id of a gate this one replaces, if any. An active gate may only move to deprecated in the same PR that either sets a replacement's supersedes or states in the PR body why none exists.

fail_mode.description: What this gate does when it cannot correctly evaluate its own condition (crash, timeout, unreachable dependency, malformed input) -- distinct from a confirmed policy violation, which always denies by definition. Absent means not yet assessed; never assume fail-closed by default from absence alone. 'mixed' is for a gate whose branches differ; rationale must say which branch is which.

target.description: The machine-comparable subset of what trigger describes in prose: the concrete tool/pattern/path/event this gate actually targets. Absent means not yet backfilled, not 'targets nothing'. trigger remains the human-readable prose description; this field does not replace it. 'runtime-resolved-reference' (issue #1232) is for a target whose identity is not decidable from committed source at all: it is only resolvable at runtime from live platform state (e.g. a GitHub API read) or an arbitrary per-instance pointer recorded elsewhere (an issue body, a secret's value, an arbitrary file/commit pair) -- distinct from 'github-native', which is a fixed platform *setting* (e.g. branch protection), not a per-instance value.

bypass_review_status.description: Whether this gate's known-bypass surface has been reviewed at all, independent of what was found. Backfilled to 'not-yet-reviewed' for every currently-registered gate as part of issue #1231: a mechanical, zero-judgment default, not a claim that no gate has been reviewed for bypasses in some other, undocumented sense. Deliberately excludes 'reviewed-found-listed-below' (issue #1232, adversarial review): that value would name a known_bypasses array that is not yet a field in this schema at all, so a schema-valid gate could claim its bypasses are listed with nowhere for them to actually be -- a misleading claim additionalProperties: false cannot catch on its own. Re-add the value in the same change that adds known_bypasses and a regression test proving both ship together, not before.

allOf.$comment: planes carries an explicit type: array inside the `if`. Draft 2020-12 ignores `contains` on a non-array instance, so a plain typo ("planes": "ci") would otherwise satisfy the `if` vacuously and fire the then-branch -- telling the author to add local_invocation and drop local_exclusion, the exact opposite of what a CI-only gate needs. The instance is rejected either way (planes is separately typed as an array), so this is a diagnostics fix, not a fail-open one. No separate local_stdin -> local_invocation clause is needed: the then-branch already requires local_invocation whenever the gate is on the local plane, and the else-branch already forbids local_stdin whenever it is not, so a third clause only duplicated the same error message twice on the one shape it caught.
